correctness.rationale: Under the stated Carleson/Stolz and off-log-cut hypotheses, z↦z^(rp) is locally conformal at 1 and retains an interpolating tail after collision fibers are grouped. The normalized Hardy kernels at distinct powered nodes form a Riesz sequence. Splitting t_(pk+a)=r(pk+a)+tau_a then reduces the infinite frame inequalities to uniform finite-fiber matrices M_xi=(z_j^(ra+tau_a)); only finitely many fibers have size >1, while singleton weights stay uniformly bounded below. Small tau_a=a*epsilon gives Vandermonde columns on z_j^(r+epsilon), whose pair differences split to first order whenever z_i^r=z_j^r. Lagrange inverse bounds yield smallest singular value at least c epsilon^(m_r-1); a moment-canceling vector in a maximally colliding subcluster matches this rate from above. Therefore A_epsilon is Theta(epsilon^(2(m_r-1))) and B_epsilon is Theta(1). A fiber with >p nodes cannot have rank p; a sufficiently large finite period always avoids this obstruction. Independently checked 2-/3-node collision exponents, not substituted for infinite proof.
